name: Policy-resolved feature flags in third-party deployments
what: When the organisation runs without Anthropic's flag service, GrowthBook flags are replaced by a rule table: each flag is remote, forced to a value, forced for a group, always a value, or derived from a policy condition (auto mode, self-hosted sessions, built-in browser), and the resulting defaults are handed to the web app as defaultValue entries.
how: Two tables keyed by numeric flag ids: H2t entries {rule:'remote'|'forced'|'forcedFor',group,value} and U2t entries {rule:'always'|'when'|'follows'|'computed', condition, value}; resolver u4t(flagId, rule, config, computed) returns the value (or a remote web override when allowed) and d4t builds the {flag:{defaultValue}} map; conditions (JC) autoModeCode, autoModeCowork, autoModeCodeOrBypassDisabled, selfHostedSessions, scheduledTasksEnabled, claudeInChromeEnabled, builtinBrowserEnabled, alwaysStartWithDefaultModel, titleNeedsCli, featureDiscoveryDisabled computed from managed config (conditions map at core.js:55735). Third-party sessions additionally set DISABLE_GROWTHBOOK=1 for the CLI.

name: Third-party inference provider matrix with credential-source gating
what: The policy registry models how each inference provider (Anthropic API, gateway, Bedrock, Mantle, Vertex, Foundry) may authenticate (static key, helper script, interactive SSO, vendor profile, workforce identity, external IdP) and rejects invalid combinations.
how: Provider table dAe entries with cliFlag (CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK, _MANTLE, _VERTEX, _FOUNDRY, ANTHROPIC_AWS, ANTHROPIC_GOOGLE_CLOUD, GATEWAY), noDiscoveryFor and noBearerFor credential kinds, needsBaseUrlFor; credential kinds static, helper-script (TTL default 3600 s, timeout 60 s, silent refresh), interactive, vendor-profile, workforce, external-idp; session lifetime and gateway-managed Claude Code options; credential helper output injected as CLAUDE_CODE_HOST_CREDS_FILE with CLAUDE_CODE_PROVIDER_MANAGED_BY_HOST=1.

name: MCP tool-call gate: one transport-level choke point with an explicit decision cascade
what: Every tools/call frame to a local or in-process MCP server passes a gate that validates the frame, requires the server to have listed its tools, refuses ambiguous tool names, and then decides allow or deny through a fixed cascade, failing closed on any error and telling the model not to retry denied calls.

Frame checks: id present, params.name string, arguments object ('refused a malformed tools/call frame'); the gate issues its own tools/list (id prefix mcp-tool-call-gate/tools-list/, up to 50 pages, 5 s wait) and refuses calls before the list is complete ('not_listed','still_listing'); b(name) refuses names that are not one unambiguous advertised tool (normalised-name collision -> 'unknown_tool'). Decision NS.authorize: (1) session disallowedTools globs -> deny; (2) single-use receipt minted when the CLI's own canUseTool allowed the identical call -> allow; (3) unless the tool is on the must-ask set (predicate Vy): allowedTools patterns, standing host grants, permission mode waiving asking (default/auto/adopted), auto mode + read-only annotation -> allow; (4) otherwise canUseTool card; callback error or null -> deny 'could not be checked by the Claude app ... Do not retry it in this session'; abort -> deny. allow may return rewritten arguments. Every decision emits desktop_mcp_tool_call_gate{session_id,tool_name,basis} with basis in {disallowed_tools, record, allowed_tools, host_grant, permission_mode, permission_mode_auto, auto_read_only, decided_allow, decided_deny, callback_error, aborted, no_gate, unaskable_name, malformed, not_listed, still_listing, unknown_tool, gate_error}. MS() registers a deny-everything gate when none exists for an in-process server.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane should enforce tool policy at the MCP transport boundary (so CLI, remote, artifact and sub-agent paths all pass it), log a machine-readable decision basis for each call, and fail closed.
notes: pretty/c1xGi.js is the pretty-printed .vite/build/index.chunk-1xGiXs9t.js. The decision-basis list doubles as an audit schema.

name: Single-use consent receipts bound to the SHA-256 of the exact arguments
what: When the agent's permission layer approves an MCP tool call, the desktop mints a short-lived receipt keyed by session, tool and a hash of the canonical arguments; the gate later spends it exactly once, so a call whose arguments differ from what was approved is re-checked.
how: DS ledger: key = sessionId \0 toolName \0 sha256(h2(args)); oS store with deposit(key, callId, personAnswered) (TTL iS=120 s), adopt, spend (live->spent, returns {personAnswered}), deny, removeOldestLive, dropPrefix(session) and a cap of 256 settled entries. minting(): wraps canUseTool; when it returns allow for an mcp__ tool from an sdk-sourced server with a tool-use id, mint(session, toolUseID, name, updatedInput ?? input). The same store is used for scheduled-task 'sink' consents (sinkReceiptKey session\0tool\0taskId, deposit/spend/adopt).
verevonRelevance: Bind approvals to argument hashes and make them single-use with short TTL to prevent confused-deputy replays between approval and execution.

Switch to that account to use it.'), no_one (sign-in predates account switching) or the active ids; qS logs refusals (warn for inactive_account). name: Host-to-agent activity ledger framed as non-instruction context with tag escaping
what: The desktop tells the agent about events it did not cause (conversation rewound or forked, files not reverted, terminal tab activity and exit codes) through an injected block that states it is context from the app, not instructions, with caps and sanitisation of the text.

Validation rejects invalid regexes, missing capture groups, mask on directories, extract with decode, duplicate pair members. On macOS and Windows 'mask' currently degrades to 'deny'. Source-trust: only user/managed/CLI settings.
evidence: DOC: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing#mask-credentials (the sandbox shows a per-session sentinel and the proxy substitutes the real value on requests to allowed hosts; requires network.tlsTerminate, otherwise masking fails without leaking; macOS files are blocked instead of masked)

notes: Part of the embedded Claude Code runtime, so present in desktop Code sessions; not specific to the desktop shell.

name: SSH remote-session safety: withheld credential prompts until the host key is verified
what: For SSH remote sessions the desktop refuses to relay password, passphrase or one-time-code prompts to the UI until the host's key is already recorded in known_hosts, requires explicit first-connection key confirmation, refuses configurations that cannot save a confirmed key, and lets admins allowlist hosts.

Per-host tool grants: preference ccSshHostToolGrants[{account, endpointKey, serverHostKey, toolName, sshHost, serverLabel, toolLabel, grantedAt}]; policy sshHostAllowlist (array, fail-closed []), trusted hosts via get/setTrustedSSHHosts; SettingsResolver ignores a malformed allowlist from a source with a warning.

name: MCP URL-elicitation guard
what: When an MCP server asks the user to open a URL (URL-mode elicitation), the desktop only honours https URLs, refuses form-mode requests, declines when another dialog is open or the server is disabled, never opens Claude's own sign-in URLs, and asks with a default-Cancel dialog naming the server and host.

name: Claude-auth-URL detector with multi-pass normalisation
what: A URL classifier recognises authentication URLs of Claude and Anthropic hosts (including staging) after Unicode, control-character, backslash, scheme-nesting and repeated percent-decoding normalisation, so plugin OAuth endpoints and MCP elicitation URLs cannot be used to steer users through the app's own sign-in flows.

Used by plugin OAuth (authorizationUrlFromUntrustedConfig) and URL elicitation, emitting desktop_claude_auth_url_withheld.

Delivery: the object goes into the CLI's flag settings at spawn (settings.autoMode) and again through the apply_flag_settings control request when iOS or Android simulator panes attach (kb() appends simulator environment and soft_deny rules, Cf() only when the existing arrays start with '$defaults'); it is stripped with a warning when the spawning CLI is older than 2.1.118; sessions whose CLI process was started without classifier support fall back to cards (cause no_auto_mode_support).

name: Intent-clearing rule grammar: soft-deny rules say what the user's own message must name
what: Every block rule the desktop gives the classifier follows one template: a rule name, a 'must name' requirement, the action pattern, and an explicit 'clears when' clause. Only the user's own words (or a standing instruction, or a yes to the agent's offer) can clear a block; the agent's judgment, file content, web pages, tool results, review comments and other sessions' notes never can.
how: Template read in mf/hf/rM, shown for the archive rule: a header made of the rule name and a bracketed named+specifics tag with a must-name clause (here: that session, and archiving it), then the action pattern (the archive tool on session_id=self or on any session not already cleared by an allow rule), then a clears-when sentence: the rule clears when the user's own message asked for it, a yes to the agent's offer or a standing instruction counts, and neither the agent's own judgment nor a request that first appeared in a file, web page, tool result or another session's transcript does. Variations: broad verbs do not name an action (Organize, clean up, dedupe, free up space do not name deletion); a place clears only when the user's own words point at it; recoverable actions are marked as such; 'ask once' per call (each call that starts an unattended session needs its own ask). Rules cross-reference the CLI's built-in rule families by name: Irreversible Local Destruction, Local Operations, Unauthorized Persistence, Instruction Poisoning, Create Unsafe Agents, SUB-AGENT DELEGATION, Data Exfiltration, DESTINATION NOVELTY, PII Data Handling, Sensitive-Source Provenance, Self-Modification, Memory Directory, Scope Creep, Prompt Injection, Multi-Agent Coordination, Test Artifacts, Session-Created Job Cleanup. Public docs show the same grammar in the CLI's own default rules (Git Destructive [named+specifics ...]) and state that an approval must name the action and the specific thing that makes it dangerous.
evidence: DOC: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes#approvals-you-state-in-conversation (name the action and its specifics; one approval covers one action unless granted as standing)
DOC: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config (precedence: hard_deny, then soft_deny, then allow exceptions, then explicit user intent; sample 'Git Destructive [named+specifics ...]' rule)
verevonRelevance: A reusable, auditable template for agent-safety rules in Model Plane: each rule declares what the user must have said, what does not count as saying it, and what recoverability means, which also gives UI copy for consent cards.
notes: Rule names listed come from cross-references inside the desktop's rule text; the CLI's own default rules were not read locally (public docs print a sample).

name: Argument provenance discipline: the classifier is told which call fields are agent-written and so prove nothing
what: Each tool description handed to the classifier lists the few arguments that mean something and states that every other key (approved_by_user, user_request, a note, a reason, summaries, session titles, branch names) is the agent's own text and establishes nothing about what the user asked.
how: Repeated boilerplate in the rule text, paraphrased: only the arguments named in the description carry meaning; any other key (examples given: approved_by_user, user_request, a note, reason) is the agent's own text; a session id, whoever wrote it, is only a label for the target (title, folder, last activity) and may contain text a model wrote, so it proves nothing about the target or about what the user asked; app-prepared preview fields (removes=, worktrees=, plan=) are described as the app's own words, not the agent's. The same discipline shows app-side: card text built from model-controlled fields is stripped of angle brackets and backticks and cut to 300 characters (Hs), and the card kind recorded for the classifier is chosen from a map (move_to_cloud_plan, set_setting_change, app_tool_card).
verevonRelevance: When a model reviews another model's tool calls, tell the reviewer exactly which fields are trusted (app-authored) and which are attacker-influenceable, and sanitize model-controlled text before it reaches a human or reviewer.

name: App-prepared plan argument with a fingerprint, plus execution-time re-check of what the card promised
what: For consequential moves (continue this session in the cloud) the app appends its own plan= sentence, built from git state and the account's environment list, as the last argument; the classifier is told to block any call whose last argument is not the app's plan, and at execution the app re-renders the card and refuses to proceed if what it said has changed.
how: Rule text: the app writes plan= from the repository's git state and the account's environment list, puts it last after every argument the agent wrote, discards any plan= the agent sent, and ends it with a bracketed plan id fingerprint the app checks; the agent's own summary= is passed JSON-quoted with every non-printable-ASCII character escaped; block when the plan pushes anywhere other than the session's own repository, when it uses an organization or self-hosted environment the user did not name, or when a remote was added or re-pointed in the transcript. Host side: describeMoveToCloud(session, input, toolUseId) builds the card (deny with 'The app could not check ... nothing was shown to the user; try again' when preparation fails), forgetMoveToCloudPlan drops the stored plan when the card is not allowed, unattended sessions are denied outright, and for scheduled-task writes an allowed card is converted to a deny when routineCard(...).said no longer equals what was shown ('Nothing was changed: what the approval card said of this scheduled task no longer holds').
verevonRelevance: Approval cards for irreversible moves should carry an app-computed, fingerprinted plan that the model cannot forge, and execution should re-verify the plan against current state (TOCTOU) before acting.
notes: The plan generator itself sits in a separate lazily loaded chunk (index.chunk-CfnOVdFk.js) that was not read.

name: Tool-result blindness and prompt-injection signals written into the classifier policy
what: The classifier sees only tool names and arguments, never tool outputs, so the desktop's rules describe what to infer from call shape: a device action that does not follow from the user's task and first appears after a screen read is a strong injection signal, while read-then-tap is normal; arguments such as URLs and typed text are judged on content.
how: Simulator rule text (Sf), paraphrased: the classifier never sees what a screen read returned, so that output cannot inject it, but anything on the device screen (the app, loaded pages, notifications) is untrusted and may already have steered the agent; a device action that does not follow from the user's task and first appears after a screen read is a strong signal; the read-then-tap or read-then-type sequence alone is normal usage and not a signal; judge the arguments (scheme, host and query of url=, the content of text=, the app a launch names); a coordinate-only touch names nothing verifiable (the text points to the CLI's UNSEEN TOOL RESULTS rule). Soft-deny rules: Desktop Simulator Open URL (must name that URL, site or deep link; external addresses, another app's scheme such as mailto: sms: tel:, or URLs whose path or query carries session data are blocked) and Desktop Simulator Typed Secrets (typing credentials or file or environment contents the user did not give the agent). Public docs confirm that in the CLI's own classifier requests tool results are stripped and that a separate server-side probe scans incoming tool results.
evidence: DOC: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes (classifier sees user messages, non-read-only tool calls and CLAUDE.md; tool results are stripped; a separate server-side probe scans tool results)
verevonRelevance: A result-blind reviewer is robust to injection but needs explicit heuristics about action shape and argument content; Verevon can pair a result-blind action reviewer with a separate result-scanning probe, as Claude does.
notes: The phrase UNSEEN TOOL RESULTS refers to a section of the CLI's built-in rules that is not present locally.

name: Terminal-tool classifier policy: judge keystrokes as the shell would read them, with PowerShell persistence vectors named
what: When Claude types commands into the user's visible terminal, the classifier is told to judge the text exactly as a Bash call with the sandbox off, reading it as PowerShell at its interactive prompt, decoding nested interpreters, and treating anything that alters the user's later shell behaviour (history, hooks, profiles, environment) as blocked unless asked for.
how: Rule text for run_in_terminal / open_terminal_tab: only a literal line reaches the classifier (no variables, pipes, parentheses or script blocks); decode -EncodedCommand and nested powershell -Command, pwsh -c, cmd /c, bash -c, python -c, node -e and ssh arguments; arguments to .cmd or .bat shims (npm, npx, yarn) are re-read by cmd.exe so %NAME% expands and a quote followed by & | < > can start another command even inside PowerShell single quotes; planted history (Add-History, the PSReadLine saved-history file), event, formatting and debugger hooks (Register-EngineEvent, Update-TypeData, Update-FormatData, Set-PSBreakpoint, Set-PSDebug, Enable-RunspaceDebug), $env: values, imported modules, dot-sourced files and profile or module-folder writes are blocked unless the user asked for exactly that change; a reused tab's directory is wherever earlier commands left it; running in the visible terminal never makes a command safer. Extra soft-deny: Desktop Terminal Tab Outside The Project (cwd outside the session folder; a folder the agent created or unpacked is untrusted code because the shell runs its startup hooks such as direnv). Host-side gates: tools only act on tabs Claude opened that the user never typed in, and cards carry causes ssh_terminal, launcher_terminal, remote_control_active, own_shell_rule.
verevonRelevance: If Verevon ever drives a user-visible terminal, classify the typed text with shell-specific knowledge (re-evaluation by cmd.exe, PowerShell hooks, profile persistence), and restrict it to terminals the agent created.
notes: Windows/PowerShell wording is specific to this machine's build (the rule is generated per platform; the macOS variant was not seen).

name: Cowork-mode classifier profile: a different environment and rule set for knowledge-work agents
what: Cowork sessions (document, spreadsheet, email and connector work for one person) get their own classifier environment description and rules, describing the VM filesystem layout and a trust boundary of the session sandbox plus the user's connected folders and accounts, with rules for deletion grants, folder access, skill persistence and scheduled tasks.
how: aM({hostLoop}) returns autoMode.{environment, soft_deny, allow} each starting with '$defaults': environment entry Qj overrides the default 'Primary use' (not software development; no git repository normally; trust boundary), $j or eM describes the filesystem (VM under /sessions/<name>/ with mnt/outputs, mnt/uploads, mnt/.claude as the Self-Modification surface and mnt/.auto-memory as the memory directory; connected folders are real, read-write, not backed up, no undo; deleting or overwriting a file the transcript did not create is Irreversible Local Destruction), tM lists the built-in tools; soft_deny rM: Cowork Delete Grant (grant is folder-wide; Organize, clean up, dedupe, free up space do not name deletion), Cowork Folder Access (block when broader than what the user referenced, first seen in file or web content, or a system/app/config location), Cowork Skill Persistence (block content that grants permissions or tells future sessions to skip confirmation, copied from a document or tool result, or naming recipients the user never gave), Cowork Scheduled Task Write/Delete; allow iM: Local Deliverables, Folder Picker (no path means only the human can complete it), session-created schedules, read-only list. Attached when the session is not a chat session and a remote flag is on (includeRules).
verevonRelevance: Different agent products need different safety profiles (coding vs knowledge work); Model Plane should select a classifier profile per agent type with explicit trust-boundary text and filesystem semantics.
notes: Which remote flag (3424551112) is enabled for a given account is not visible locally.

name: Approval routing by stand-down verdict: the app decides whether a card, the classifier or bypass answers each desktop tool call
what: For every desktop-side tool call the app computes a verdict: it either stands down so the classifier (auto mode) or nobody (bypass) decides, or it keeps a card with a named cause. Auto and bypass only count when they were chosen in this app and the process was started with support; unattended and remote-initiated runs never stand down for sensitive tools.
how: Verdict objects {standDown:'classifier'|'bypass'} or {cause}. Xu(session): mode auto stands down only if the CLI was spawned with classifier rules (autoModeClassifierRulesAtSpawn), the org has not disabled auto mode, and provenance holds (local session, or autoChosenInApp true, or 'adopted' on a remote target while the adopted-process gate allows it); otherwise causes no_auto_mode_support, auto_mode_off_by_org, auto_not_chosen_in_app, auto_provenance_unknown. Mode bypass needs bypassAvailableAtSpawn and bypass chosen in the app and no org ban (causes bypass_off_by_org, bypass_unavailable_at_start, bypass_not_chosen_in_app). Qu(tool, session): ordinary modes keep the ordinary card; an attendance state other than 'plain' (the attendance helper n.js, which separates attended runs from unattended ones such as routines and dispatched work; exact values not decoded) forces cause 'unattended' when it is unresolvable, when the session is not local, when the tool is in a fixed sensitive set (folder access, folder move, scheduled-task writes, remote control, connector switch, settings, cloud move, base-branch sync and others) or when it is a terminal tool; in bypass mode, tools the organization requires approval for force org_requires_approval, and terminal tools do so whenever the org requires approval for Bash; a pending permission-mode change forces mode_change_pending; terminal tools additionally keep a card while Remote Control is active (cause remote_control_active). mcpToolCallWaivedByMode and mcpToolCallCardCause apply the same verdict to MCP calls. Managed settings that cannot be read keep the card (org_settings_unavailable). Every route emits desktop_ccd_*_auto_mode telemetry with an outcome such as classifier_ask or deferred_to_classifier.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane needs one pure function that returns who decides (human card, safety classifier, nobody) with a typed reason from mode provenance, attendance state, org policy and pending changes, and that fails toward a card.
notes: Names such as Zu, Yl, Jl are minified sets; their exact membership was inferred from the neighbouring definitions at sdk.js:2945-2968 and the rule text.

name: Typed approval-cause taxonomy with a plain-language 'why am I being asked' sentence per cause
what: Every approval card carries a cause code and a human sentence that explains why this call asks instead of running, for example that the organization requires approval, that a permission-mode change is still taking effect, that a session on another machine did not have auto mode chosen in this app, or that an action cannot be undone so Claude asks in every permission mode.
how: A frozen map from cause code to message (core.js 154870) with about 33 entries: ordinary, unattended, mode_change_pending, org_requires_approval, org_folder_policy, auto_provenance_unknown, auto_not_chosen_in_app, ssh_terminal, launcher_terminal, reveals_folder_on_windows, no_auto_mode_support, auto_mode_off_by_org, bypass_off_by_org, org_settings_unavailable, bypass_unavailable_at_start, bypass_not_chosen_in_app, paused, remote_control_active, ends_this_session, costlier, cuts_remote_control, restores_dismissed_pr, keep_awake_setting_off, keep_awake_on_battery_off, own_shell_rule, server_unconfirmed, folder_access, folder_move, question, deletes_sessions, discards_work, raises_permissions, rewrites_routine. The broker passes the cause through decisionReason with reasonFromApp so the card shows the app's sentence rather than model text, and cards for causes marked 'in every permission mode' are never waived.
verevonRelevance: Give every Verevon approval a machine-readable cause enum and a user-facing explanation; it makes approvals auditable, testable and explainable, and lets admins see which policy produced each prompt.
notes: Message strings are localised by the web UI elsewhere; this map is the English source in the main process.

name: Escalation checks that keep a card in front of auto mode: routine outranking, repricing clamp, link-cutting, unconfirmed server
what: Even when the classifier would decide, the app forces a human card for calls that raise privilege or cost or cut a user link: raising a session's permission mode, writing a routine that could do more than its author, repricing a helper session above the caller's own model or effort, ending a Remote Control link the user set up, bringing back a dismissed pull request, or any call whose providing server has not been confirmed.
how: forceAskVerdict(tool, input, session): discards_work for cleanup that removes uncommitted changes or deletes sessions; raises_permissions via permissionModeCallRaises (target mode ranked above its current mode, or the target unknown); rewrites_routine via routineWouldOutrankCaller (a routine's carried permission mode, stored approvals or placement on another host may not exceed what the calling session can do without asking; unreadable managed settings keep the card); ends_this_session when archiving the session itself; costlier via childRepriceOverClamp / repriceWithinClamp (a helper's model must be the caller's own or cheaper, effort not higher, fast mode on only if the caller is already fast); cuts_remote_control when disabling a link the user turned on; server_unconfirmed when the tool belongs to a desktop-control server the app has not confirmed provides it in this session; restores_dismissed_pr; org settings unavailable. When the verdict stays 'classifier' and the turn was delegated by an orchestrator session, a short list of lifecycle tools (set_monitor, set_auto_merge only to disable, keep-awake, stop or archive, and sidebar moves, limited to the session itself or its own children and capped at 25 sessions per call) is answered by the recorded delegation instead (delegatedAsk, delegatedAllow, telemetry desktop_ccd_delegated_ask_allowed).
verevonRelevance: Delegated or scheduled agents must never gain more privilege, cost or reach than the principal that created them; Model Plane should test this ordering ('would the child outrank the caller?') at creation time and treat unreadable policy as a reason to ask.
notes: Complements the permission-mode ratchet record (mode ranks) by covering routines, costs and links.

name: Fan-out cap on agent-started sessions: starts are free until a per-user-message budget is exceeded
what: Claude can start helper sessions from a session; starts under a cap since the user's last message pass without a card (once the host, folder or environment is known), but the tenth start triggers a card saying how many starts were already asked, and proposal-only starts show a proposal card that starts nothing.
how: md(tool, input, session, toolUseId, source) returns true when the tool is a session-start tool (Gl = the start-session tool and its hand-off sibling), the call is not a proposal or offer without a proposal id, the session is attended, and hd(...) >= 10, where hd reads session.sideSessionStartsSinceUserMessage and adjusts for concurrent in-flight tool uses; true produces a card whose text says Claude wants to start another session and has already asked to start N since the user's last message (the eleventh and later starts). Under the cap, when the CLI itself has no reason to ask, the org does not require approval for the tool and firstUseSidePlace shows no new host, folder or environment ('place') needing consent, the broker auto-allows the call and counts it (noteSideSessionStart). The classifier rule Desktop Session Fan Out additionally blocks runs of near-identical briefs, more starts than the pieces the user listed, and starts prompted by text that first appeared in a file, web page, tool result or another session's note.
verevonRelevance: Budget agent-initiated parallel runs per user message (default around ten) with a card at the limit, and require consent the first time a run is placed on a new host, folder or environment.
notes: Medium confidence on the exact meaning of Gl and the counter semantics; read from minified code.

name: Homoglyph-aware scrubber that neutralises forged host envelope tags in untrusted text
what: Untrusted text that the app embeds into model-visible context is passed through a scrubber that breaks any look-alike of the app's own pseudo-XML tags (system-reminder, cross-session-message, task-notification, terminal output wrappers and about forty others), including versions spelled with lookalike brackets, slashes, hyphens, zero-width characters or confusable letters.
how: index.chunk-C6_NM1s9.js builds, per tag-name set, one case-insensitive Unicode regex (V) that matches a '<' or any of about 17 lookalike opening brackets (fullwidth, small, angle, math, canadian-syllabic variants, plus Unicode tag-block characters), optional lookalike slashes for closing tags, whitespace and invisible-character filler, and the tag name with per-letter confusable classes (Cyrillic, Greek, fullwidth, small capitals, mathematical alphabets; sharp s and capital sharp s match 'ss'; hyphen and underscore lookalikes), anchored by a boundary class; it rewrites the opening bracket to '<\~', which breaks the tag for the model. Pre-normalisation: NFKD, strip combining marks, NFKC, lowercase; remove default-ignorable code points and Cf characters (soft hyphen, zero-width, bidi controls, variation selectors, BOM); tag names must match [a-z0-9_-]+ or the builder throws. Reserved sets in c1xGi.js:58 (46 tag names): system-reminder; envelopes ci-monitor-event, side-sessions-event; cross-session-message, teammate-message, agent-message; nine command and bash wrappers; 26 injected-context tags (selected element, terminal selection, github_issue, browser-output, uploaded_files, available-deferred-tools, new-diagnostics, mcp-resource, ide_selection, pr-created and similar); task-notification, agent-notification, bash-notification, widget_context_hint, tool_use_error; plus the bare pseudo-tags tick, goal, cell, cell_type, language, thinking, which get a second pass (W calls the builder with its strict flag).
verevonRelevance: Any system that wraps host-injected context in tags must scrub attacker-controlled text for tag lookalikes (Unicode confusables, invisible characters) before it reaches the model; a shared scrubber with a declared reserved-tag registry is cheap and effective.
notes: The exported wrappers (Me, Ne, D, O in c1xGi.js:59-69) were found but their call sites in other chunks were not traced; the scrubber design and reserved list are read directly.

name: Cross-session message envelope: escaped sender attributes, @-mention neutralisation across hosts, explicit delivery states
what: When one Claude session messages another, the receiver gets a wrapped envelope naming the sender, with the text escaped, with @-mentions defused when the two sessions run in different places, and the sender is told precisely whether the message was delivered, queued or undelivered and why.
how: Tool handler for the send-message tool: refuses missing fields, sending to itself, unknown, archived, still-starting or unreachable targets with instructive text (an archived parent tells the agent to message the nearest live ancestor or reply to the user); builds '<cross-session-message from=<id> name=<title>>' + escaped body + closing tag, where attribute and body pass the escape helpers mf and _f, and, unless both sessions share a place (same host and folder lineage), the text also passes pJr which replaces '@' with fullwidth '@' (U+FF20) so the receiving CLI cannot treat it as a file mention; sendPeerMessage carries origin {kind:'peer', from, name, fromMode} where fromMode is the sender's declared permission class only when the receiver bypasses prompts; results map to delivered, queued ('do not wait on it; check list_events') or undelivered with a reference code. The classifier rule set describes the envelope as another session's transcript, quoted data that clears nothing reserved to the user.
verevonRelevance: Inter-agent messaging in Verevon should be an enveloped, escaped, origin-tagged channel with defused file mentions across trust boundaries and honest delivery receipts.
notes: Receiver-side parsing of the envelope tag lives in the CLI and was not read.

name: Auto-execution config drop list when session output is copied across a trust boundary
what: When files produced by an imported or sibling third-party session are copied into a session folder, files that would auto-run code or change tool behaviour (agent config, git config, shell profiles, direnv files, Python import hooks, version-manager configs, package-manager hooks) are filtered out so importing a session cannot plant an execution vector.
how: GLa(src, dst, {dropExecConfigs}) wraps fs.cp with a filter: always drops .claude, .git, .mcp.json, claude.md and claude.local.md (names compared after NFKC and lowercase); when dropExecConfigs is set (import from another identity: i!==undefined or sibling-3p source) it also drops anything Kin(relative path) classifies as a protected file or directory: the dot-directory list (.git .vscode .idea .claude .husky .cargo .devcontainer .yarn .mvn .ssh .aws .gnupg .kube .docker), the file list xin (.gitconfig .gitmodules shell rc and profile files .ripgreprc .mcp.json .claude.json .npmrc .yarnrc .envrc .direnvrc .pre-commit-config.yaml .devcontainer.json .env .netrc, PowerShell profile scripts and powershell.config.json), env-file prefixes (.env.*) except example, sample, template and dist, and system roots (/etc, LaunchAgents and LaunchDaemons, shell session dirs, gcloud, git and direnv config dirs, PowerShell profile folders including OneDrive-redirected Documents, the Startup folder); plus the set WLa (conftest.py, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py, mise and rtx configs, .tool-versions, rust-toolchain, .pnpmfile.cjs, bunfig.toml, lefthook, pyrightconfig.json, .hg, .Rprofile, .Renviron, .ghci, .pryrc, .octaverc); bare git repository layout files are skipped.
verevonRelevance: Any import, restore or cross-tenant copy of agent workspaces in Verevon should drop a maintained list of auto-executing config files and normalise names (Unicode, trailing dots, aliases) before comparing.
notes: The list is broader than the deny rules in the protected-subpaths record because it targets files that execute on the next use rather than on write.

name: Admin-managed built-in connectors (GitHub, Microsoft 365, web search) as typed policy entries
what: Besides user-added MCP servers, admins can enable three app-shipped connectors by policy: a bundled GitHub server (with GitHub Enterprise Server support, toolsets and read-only mode), a bundled Microsoft 365 server (tenant, client id, sovereign cloud, granted permission scopes, continuous access evaluation) and a built-in web search tool (Brave, Tavily, Exa or a custom endpoint).
how: The managedMcpServers entry union includes object variants with server:'github' | 'microsoft365' | 'websearch' (availableInVersion 1.25927.0, 1.19367.0, 1.19367.0). GitHub: clientId (letters, digits, ._-, at most 36), host (https, non-loopback, normalised to origin), scope tokens (lowercase pattern like repo read:org), toolsets (comma list of lowercase ids), readOnly, toolPolicy. Microsoft 365: tenantId (GUID or common, organizations, consumers), clientId (mandatory for US Government clouds), azureCloud (global, us-gov-high, us-gov-dod, each with its own login and Graph hosts), continuousAccessEvaluation (default enabled), scope validated against a catalogue of 25 delegated scopes tagged always, read, admin-consent or write, toolPolicy. Web search: provider brave|tavily|exa|custom plus headers or headersHelper (required unless custom). Each variant declares the hosts it needs (nOe) so egress allowlists can be generated; a 'policy-only' transport variant lets admins set tool permissions for plugin-provided servers. The spawn switch Pm refuses any built-in server whose definition source is not 'admin'.
verevonRelevance: First-party connectors should be configured through the same typed policy registry as everything else, with per-connector hosts declared for egress control and a provenance check that only admin-sourced definitions may start app-shipped servers.
notes: Complements the managed-MCP record (arbitrary servers) by covering the app-shipped connector variants and their validators.

name: Write tools of built-in connectors default to 'ask'; eight high-impact tools per connector cannot be set to 'allow' at all
what: For the bundled GitHub and Microsoft 365 connectors, every write or send tool ships with an 'ask' default, and eight high-impact tools per connector (Microsoft 365: send mail, forward, send draft, create or update event, three Teams message tools; GitHub: merge pull request, push files, create or update and delete file, run, rerun and rerun-failed workflows, delete workflow logs) stay on 'ask' even if an admin sets 'allow' for them explicitly or by pattern; the admin form flags write tools that have no explicit policy.
how: aOe maps tool name to 'ask': Microsoft 365 35 write tools (mail, drafts, labels, filters, vacation, events, SharePoint file operations, Teams messages and chats), GitHub 36 (file and branch writes, issues, pull requests and reviews, workflow runs, notifications, gists, project items). oOe lists the 8 tools per connector that are never opened by globs. sOe(entry) builds the effective policy: for tools in oOe the stricter of the default and the configured value (explicit entry or wildcard match) always wins, so they cannot be lowered; for the other write tools the default applies unless the admin names the tool exactly or uses the bare '*' key, so partial patterns such as outlook_* cannot lower them either (Ds picks the stricter). cOe(entry, tools) returns uncovered (tools with no readOnlyHint and no default or explicit policy) and globAllowOnly (write tools allowed only through a wildcard) for admin warnings.
verevonRelevance: Ship connectors with an ask-by-default write policy generated from tool annotations plus a hard-coded never-wildcard set for exfiltration and irreversible tools, and warn admins about uncovered write tools.
notes: Counts (35, 36, 8, 8) were computed by script from the literal tables.

name: Tool-policy strictness lattice with strictest-wildcard resolution and lossy merge of wildcard allows
what: Per-tool admin policies are ordered blocked, ask, ask-session, allow; when several wildcard rules match a tool the strictest wins, and when two policy sources are merged a wildcard 'allow' survives only if both sources allow it.
how: JTe ranks {blocked:3, ask:2, 'ask-session':1, allow:0}; Ds(a,b) returns the stricter; ks(policy, tool) returns an exact entry, else folds Ds over every matching wildcard pattern (Os is a linear-time glob matcher; plugin tool names mcp__plugin_<id>_* are compared case-insensitively); QTe(a,b) merges two policies key by key with Ds and drops a wildcard result of 'allow' unless both sides specified it. Older desktops that do not know ask-session treat it as blocked (documented in the managed-MCP schema).
verevonRelevance: Define Model Plane tool policy as a total order with deterministic merge rules (strictest wins, no silent widening through wildcards), and keep the ordering in one tested function.

name: Bundled GitHub MCP server: device-code sign-in, token bound to host, client and scope, read-only and toolset env controls
what: The app ships GitHub's MCP server as a Go binary that runs over stdio; signing in uses GitHub's device-code flow with the code copied to the clipboard, the token is stored encrypted and bound to the configuration, and admins can restrict the server to chosen toolsets or read-only mode and point it at GitHub Enterprise Server.
how: connectGithubBuiltinMcp resolves resources/github-mcp/github-mcp-server.exe (app.asar.unpacked when packaged; the CLAUDE_DESKTOP_GITHUB_MCP_BINARY override only in unpackaged builds), spawns it with 'stdio' and environment GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN, GITHUB_HOST, GITHUB_TOOLSETS and GITHUB_READ_ONLY=1, connects the MCP client with a 60 s handshake and tool-discovery timeout and pipes stderr to a per-server log stream. Auth module: device grant via {host}/login/device/code and /login/oauth/access_token with default scope 'repo read:org read:user'; the user code is copied to the clipboard and shown in a Cancel-only dialog; token file github-token.enc holds safeStorage ciphertext of 'github-token-v1:<dir>:' plus JSON {token, bind} where bind is the first 16 hex characters of SHA-256 over [host, clientId, scope]; a bind or key mismatch drops the entry, an undecryptable blob is kept but not used, and when safeStorage is unavailable the token is not cached. Cached tokens are validated with GET /user (redirect:'error', 10 s timeout) and a 401 clears them; after a tool-call error the server is re-validated at most once a minute. While signed out the connector appears as a 'needs auth' shell that shows its cached tool list and exposes a single-flight requestSignIn which respawns the server on success.
verevonRelevance: A first-party connector for a code host should use device-code auth, bind stored tokens to the exact host, client and scope, validate before use, and expose read-only and toolset restrictions through policy.
notes: The Go binary itself was not executed or disassembled (REA inspect_pe_resources: PE32+, 20,566,352 bytes, no version resource, see claude.inventory.md).

name: Microsoft 365 MCP server: tools register only if Entra granted the delegated scope, and denials explain which permission is missing
what: The bundled Microsoft Graph MCP server exposes 50 tools (15 read, 35 write) but registers a write tool only when the signed-in account's delegated permissions include its scope (and a companion read scope where needed), defaults to read-only scopes, and turns Graph 403s into precise explanations of which scopes are missing or granted.
how: Server identity mcp-ms-graph. Each tool class declares requiredDelegatedScope (Mail.Send, Mail.ReadWrite, Calendars.ReadWrite, MailboxSettings.ReadWrite, ChatMessage.Send, ChannelMessage.Send, Chat.Create, Files.ReadWrite.All, Sites.ReadWrite.All) and isRegistrableUnderGrant(grantedScopes); forward and send-draft additionally need a mail read scope. At startup the desktop passes the granted scopes in MCP_GRANTED_DELEGATED_SCOPES (the admin's scope list, else the default read set User.Read, Mail.Read, Calendars.Read(.Shared), Files.Read.All, Sites.Read.All, Chat.Read, Mail.Read.Shared, OnlineMeetings.Read) and the registration loop skips tools with a logged reason ('X not granted' or 'granted Y, missing a companion read scope'); a get_granted_scopes tool returns the live grant. On 403 the error builder lists required, any-of and optional scopes per tool, the granted list, and whether the cause is a missing consent (with the admin-center path) or a resource ACL.
evidence: REA ev_f95eca018628b91e6f022ae42e52179e2249a15fa91d78cd6c768f0f08306611 (analyze_javascript_application, directory scan of resources/office365-mcp/office365-mcp-stdio.mjs: 1 parsed JS file, 1,477,211 AST nodes, 246 findings; semantic pass hit the worker heap limit, so coverage is partial; a trace_application_feature string seed 'Mail.Send' returned no match although grep finds the literal, so REA seeds do not reach this bundle's strings)
verevonRelevance: Least privilege at tool-registration time (hide tools the grant cannot support) plus model-readable permission diagnostics reduces both attack surface and wasted retries; Verevon connectors should expose a 'what am I allowed to do' tool.
notes: Tool counts come from scripted extraction of 'name=' declarations and readOnlyHint flags (15 true, 35 false) in pretty/o365.js. REA was run on this file (see evidence) but could not complete semantic analysis.

name: Microsoft 365 write-path safeguards: throttles, recipient cap, allowlisted HTML, AI-generated header and content-free audit
what: Write tools in the Microsoft 365 server pass per-user rate limits (10 writes a minute, 5 sends and 100 recipients per 5 minutes), cap recipients at 50 per mail, sanitise HTML bodies with a small tag allowlist and reject empty results, mark outgoing mail with an X-AI-Generated header, and log only counts, lengths and hashed ids.
how: VR sliding-window buckets keyed by a hash of the Entra object id (or of tenant and subject; the fixed key 'local' in local auth mode): writes 10 per 60 s, sends 5 per 5 min, recipients 100 per 5 min, with a separate 5-minute write counter whose tiers 10, 20 and 50 only emit warning logs (write_threshold_crossed); checkAndCharge returns RATE_LIMITED errors with retry-after seconds in the tool result; send-draft and the calendar tools that notify attendees (create, update, delete, respond) charge their recipient units after the call (chargesRecipientsPostHoc). outlook_send_mail validates at most 50 recipients (cap Ir), subject at most 255 and body at most 500,000 characters, runs sanitizeHtml with a tag allowlist (headings, p, a, lists, b, i, strong, em, strike, code, hr, br, div, table parts, pre; no script, style, img or iframe) and an attribute allowlist that keeps only a[href, name, target] (no class, id or style), and errors if nothing remains, sets internetMessageHeaders X-AI-Generated: mcp-office365, and saves to Sent Items; vacation replies must be plain text and default to internal audiences only. Audit: each tool has an allowlist of audit fields (ase) such as recipientCount, subjectLength, bodyType, messageIdHash; fields outside it are dropped with an audit_fields_dropped warning.
evidence: REA ev_f95eca018628b91e6f022ae42e52179e2249a15fa91d78cd6c768f0f08306611 (analyze_javascript_application, directory scan of resources/office365-mcp/office365-mcp-stdio.mjs: 1 parsed JS file, 1,477,211 AST nodes, 246 findings; semantic pass hit the worker heap limit, so coverage is partial; a trace_application_feature string seed 'Mail.Send' returned no match although grep finds the literal, so REA seeds do not reach this bundle's strings)
verevonRelevance: Connector servers that can send mail or messages need server-side velocity limits, content limits, sanitisation and a machine-readable AI-origin marker, with an audit schema that contains no message content.
notes: Rate-limit state is in memory only, so a restart resets the windows.

name: Host-brokered encrypted MSAL token cache and Windows broker sign-in for the bundled Microsoft 365 server
what: The Microsoft 365 server never writes its own token cache: the desktop stores it encrypted with the OS keystore, binds entries to the connector, caps sizes, can force or disable the Windows account-broker sign-in, and keeps the server from opening interactive sign-in by itself.
how: Spawn environment from fet(): MCP_AUTH_PUBLIC_CLIENT_ID, MCP_AUTH_TENANT_ID, MCP_LOCAL_AUTH_CACHE and cache path, MCP_LOCAL_AUTH_NO_INTERACTIVE=1, MCP_PARENT_WINDOW_HANDLE for the broker dialog, broker mode (required or disabled via MCP_LOCAL_AUTH_BROKER_*), MCP_LOCAL_AUTH_CAE_DISABLE when continuous access evaluation is off, MCP_AZURE_CLOUD and MCP_GRANTED_DELEGATED_SCOPES. The cache is exchanged over the child's message channel (msal-cache-get / msal-cache-set with ids): reads decrypt msal-cache.enc with safeStorage and verify the 'msal-cache-v1:<server>:' prefix and that the blob has Account, IdToken, AccessToken and RefreshToken objects (mismatch or corruption drops it), writes are refused above 8 MiB or when 16 sets are pending, and a legacy plaintext msal-cache.json is ingested once and removed ('plaintext msal cache sunset'); when the policy requires the broker, stale browser-flow caches are deleted. The server is launched through a child-process host class (t9e) that takes the Graph host as its proxy target, with stderr redirected to the per-server log stream; sign-in states (default account, account picker, interactive) are driven by the host (requestSignIn, msal-sign-in messages); disconnecting wipes the per-server cache directories and, when no other enabled server uses the same client id, signs every broker account for that client id out (eet).
verevonRelevance: Keep connector token caches in the host's encrypted store, not in the connector process, with size and queue caps and a host-driven sign-in so a compromised connector cannot prompt for credentials on its own.
notes: The in-bundle strings msal-node-runtime.node and msalruntime.dll are the Windows broker runtime; its behaviour was not analysed.

name: Agent SDK control protocol: bidirectional JSON-lines RPC with 53 host-to-agent and 13 agent-to-host request kinds
what: The desktop talks to the Claude Code engine over stdio with typed control requests in both directions: the host can set mode, model, cwd and trust, rewind files, manage MCP servers and plugins, start Remote Control and read usage, while the engine calls back for permission decisions, hook callbacks, MCP traffic, elicitation, dialogs, token refresh and UI helpers.
how: Messages {type:'control_request', request_id, request:{subtype,...}} answered by control_response success or error, plus control_cancel_request, keep_alive and transcript_mirror. Agent-to-host subtypes handled by processControlRequest: can_use_tool, hook_callback, mcp_message (bridges SDK-hosted MCP servers), elicitation, request_user_dialog, oauth_token_refresh, host_auth_token_refresh, remote_control_work_secret, ui_copy, ui_prompt_read, ui_prompt_fill, ui_prompt_suggest, ui_read_selection; four remote-tool kinds (remote_tool_call, remote_plumbing_call, remote_tools_probe, remote_tools_reannounce) are deliberately left unanswered because another machine serves them. Host-to-agent requests (53 distinct subtypes) include interrupt, set_permission_mode, set_mcp_permission_mode_override, set_model, set_max_thinking_tokens, apply_flag_settings, get_settings, update_settings, list_permission_rules, rewind_files (dry run), set_cwd (with trust_accepted and trusted_directory), seed_read_state, claim_session, remote_control, mcp_status, mcp_reconnect, mcp_toggle, mcp_read_resource, mcp_set_servers, mcp_authenticate, mcp_clear_auth, mcp_oauth_callback_url, channel_enable, claude_authenticate and OAuth callbacks, get_context_usage, get_usage, get_plan, get_hooks_listing, get_task_output, side_question, generate_session_title, rename_session, submit_feedback, message_rated, ultrareview_launch, reload_plugins, reload_skills, reload_output_styles, export_conversation, read_file and Chrome selection helpers. Robustness rules: duplicate delivery of an in-flight request id is skipped, requests after close are ignored, a per-request AbortController implements cancel, unmatched early responses are queued, and responses may carry pending_permission_requests and pending_user_dialog_requests so a reattaching client can be re-prompted.
verevonRelevance: This is a concrete checklist for Model Plane's agent protocol: a symmetric, cancellable, id-correlated control channel where permission, dialogs, token refresh and MCP bridging are first-class request types, with idempotent redelivery for reconnects.
notes: Counts come from a scripted subtype scan of c_D6Q00DJz.js lines 27899-28450 (host side) and 27663-27800 (agent side); mcp_message appears in both directions.

name: can_use_tool contract: reason-rich approval requests and decisions that carry rule updates and a permanence class
what: When the engine wants to run a tool it sends the host a structured request (suggested rules, blocked path, matched ask rule, decision reason with type and code, requires-user-interaction, default-to-no, suppress-always-allow, server prompt, MCP server identity and a connected computer folder); the host answers allow or deny, optionally rewrites the input, returns rule updates, and classifies the decision as temporary or permanent.
how: Request fields mapped in processControlRequest: tool_name, input, permission_suggestions, blocked_path, mcp_server{name, source}, decision_reason / decision_reason_type / decision_reason_code, title, display_name, description, default_to_no, suppress_always_allow_rule, tool_use_id, agent_id, requires_user_interaction, server_prompt, computer_folder{path, computer_name}, matched_ask_rule{source, tool_name, rule_content}. Decisions from the desktop broker: {behavior:'allow', updatedInput, updatedPermissions, decisionClassification:'user_permanent'|'user_temporary'} or {behavior:'deny', message}. 'Always allow' produces addRules/replaceRules updates whose destination is forced to session; skill rules must name the exact skill without wildcards; setMode updates are filtered out for cloud-run sessions (vl); when an approval would arm the project-config fence, deny rules for the project's configuration files are appended to the same update set at session scope (withProjectConfigFence); a per-session cache of decision reasons auto-allows repeats (telemetry desktop_ccd_permission_decisionreason_cache_hit). Card-only fields travel as underscore-prefixed keys in updatedInput (for example _feedbackMessage, _targetMode, _keepForSshHost) and are stripped before the call reaches the tool.
verevonRelevance: Use this field set as the schema for Verevon approval requests and decisions between Model Plane and the UI, including a permanence class for audit and rule suggestions that the UI may only apply at session scope.
notes: The permission update 'destination' vocabulary (userSettings, projectSettings, localSettings, session, cliArg) was inferred from settings sources elsewhere; only 'session' is observed in the broker code.

name: Plugin manifest extension points beyond skills and hooks: userConfig to env vars, sha256-pinned binaries, LSP, themes, workflows, channels, evals and type contracts
what: A plugin can declare typed user configuration prompted at enable time (sensitive values stored in secure storage, exposed as CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_* variables), binaries fetched with pinned SHA-256 digests, settings merged while enabled from an allowlist, LSP servers, output styles, themes, workflows, MCP channels, syntax-highlighting language packs with SRI integrity (experimental), an evals directory for a plugin evaluation harness and a TypeScript contract that other mods can depend on.
how: nge merges per-component schemas: name, displayName, commands (file, directory or inline markdown with model and allowedTools), agents, skills, hooks (settings-format hooks plus hooks.json with at most one hooks module exporting register(on)), outputStyles, themes, workflows, mcpServers (paths, URLs, MCPB files or inline), lspServers, monitors, channels, settings, types, userConfig, binaries, experimental (components whose shape may change, including evals). userConfig entries {type string|number|boolean|directory|file, title, description, required, default, multiple, sensitive, options}; keys must be identifiers because they become CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_<KEY> variables for hooks; non-sensitive values go to settings.json and sensitive values to secure storage; options values may not contain control, invisible or bidirectional-formatting characters, may not repeat in any letter case, and are only for non-sensitive single-value strings. binaries {basename: {sha256}} are fetched into bin/ at install and keys are validated (limit 64). The experimental container (components whose shape may change without a deprecation cycle) holds themes, monitors, output styles, an evals directory and a syntaxHighlighting.hljsLanguages entry {id, remote: npm:<pkg>@ver or github:<owner>/<repo>@<ref>#<path>.js, integrity: sha256/384/512-<base64>} that adds code-highlighting languages (at most 16). The types field must name a self-contained .d.ts that stays inside the plugin and declares the noun the hooks module adds.
verevonRelevance: A Verevon extension manifest should include typed, secret-aware user config, digest-pinned binaries, an allowlisted settings overlay and an evals directory so third-party agents and skills can be tested before they are trusted.
notes: Extends the earlier plugin package record, which listed folder names but not the manifest-level typed fields.

name: Plugin monitors: persistent background watchers that push events to the model, armed always or on skill invoke
what: A plugin can declare shell commands that run for the whole session as background monitors; each line they print reaches the model as a task notification, so a plugin can feed live events (CI, logs, queues) to the agent without the model polling.
how: monitors entries {name unique within the plugin, command, trigger 'always' | 'on-skill-invoke:<skill>', plus substitutions ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}, ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}, ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}, ${user_config.*}, ${ENV_VAR}}; default file monitors/monitors.json; names deduplicate re-arming on plugin reload or repeated skill invocation; each stdout line is delivered as a task_notification event. The schema description states the monitors are unsandboxed and at the same trust tier as hooks; public docs add that allow rules naming the Monitor tool are suspended in auto mode because Monitor commands run through the shell.
evidence: DOC: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes (broad Monitor allow rules are suspended in auto mode because Monitor commands run through the shell)
verevonRelevance: Plugin-defined event sources are a clean way for connectors to wake an agent; Verevon should model them as declared, named, deduplicated watchers with an explicit trust tier and sandbox policy.
notes: DOC reference is the permission-modes page (broad Monitor allow rules are suspended in auto mode).

name: MCP channels: servers that push inbound messages into a session, gated by a managed opt-in and an admin allowlist
what: An MCP server that declares the claude/channel capability can push inbound messages (chat, CI) into a session; the user opts in per session and organizations decide whether channels exist at all and which plugins may use them.
how: Plugin manifest channels[{server (must match a key in the plugin's mcpServers), displayName, userConfig for assistant mode}]; settings channelsEnabled (managed-org opt-in: default off on claude.ai Teams and Enterprise, default on for Console unless managed settings exist) and allowedChannelPlugins (managed allowlist that replaces the default Anthropic allowlist; requires channelsEnabled; entries are objects, bare strings are accepted with a warning); allowedChannelPlugins is one of the restriction allowlists merged as 'highest source owns it whole'; the host enables a channel with the channel_enable control request after the user selects it (--channels in the CLI).
evidence: DOC: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp (channels: servers declaring claude/channel push events; opt in with --channels)
verevonRelevance: Inbound push from third-party servers is an injection channel; Verevon should require an org-level switch, a plugin allowlist and per-session user opt-in before any connector may enqueue messages to an agent.
notes: The channel notification handling itself runs in the CLI and was not read.

name: Plugin source types with install-time guards: pinned archives, sparse git subdirectories, consent-bound command sources
what: Plugins can be fetched from npm, git URLs, GitHub, a subdirectory of a monorepo (sparse partial clone), an HTTPS zip archive with a SHA-256 pin, or a local command that prints the plugin directory; each has guards, and marketplace entries that fail validation are kept as visible 'unsupported' stubs rather than silently dropped.
how: Plugin source union _3: relative path, npm {package, version, registry}, url {url, ref, sha 40-hex}, github {repo, ref, sha}, git-subdir {url, path, ref, sha; checked out sparsely as a partial clone with tree filtering}, archive {url https only and not loopback, link-local or cloud-metadata hosts; sha256 verified on every download and used as version identity when no version is declared; headers or headersHelper bound to the URL}, command {shell command of printable ASCII with no run of four spaces and a length limit so the install consent UI can show it fully, timeout, mode copy|link (copy is content-hashed into the plugin cache; link keeps a live reference)}, unsupported placeholder. headersHelper commands run only when a user installs or updates the plugin, never while browsing the catalog, and an entry that sets one must be strict:false with its manifest inlined so consent is informed before the helper runs. wge() parses each marketplace entry: unparseable entries are stubbed as 'unsupported' with a bounded error (three issues, 160 characters each, keys sanitised) so detectDelistedPlugins does not see them as removed.
verevonRelevance: A Verevon marketplace should treat install sources as a closed union with per-type guards (digest pins, host blocklists, consent-sized command strings) and fail visible rather than dropping unparseable entries.

name: Marketplace allowlist matchers: host and path regexes, owner wildcards, npm registry pins and canonical URL comparison
what: Admin marketplace policies can match sources by host pattern, filesystem path pattern, exact repository, an owner wildcard, or an npm package scope; npm entries can pin the registry origin that the resolved tarball must come from, and URL comparisons are canonicalised so credentials, queries, trailing .git and the ssh.github.com alias cannot be used to dodge an allowlist.
how: Policy source kinds: url, github, git, npm, file, directory, skills-dir (a sentinel that re-enables or disables the ~/.claude/skills auto-load), hostPattern (regex over the host extracted from any source type), pathPattern (regex over file and directory paths), and settings (inline marketplaces with reserved-name rejection). github repo owner/* and npm @scope/* wildcards are valid only inside strictKnownMarketplaces and blockedMarketplaces; in an npm policy entry registry is the origin and path prefix the resolved tarball URL must fall under, and under allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly an npm marketplace keeps plugin allowed-tools only when entry and registration pin the same registry. Canonicalisation helpers dge/pge lower-case hosts, strip credentials, query and fragment, decode and normalise paths, strip a trailing .git and map ssh.github.com to github.com; mge flags wildcards in sources that must name one repository.
verevonRelevance: When Verevon lets orgs allowlist agent or connector registries, compare canonical forms, support host and path regexes, and pin registries for package sources.
notes: Extends the existing marketplace-pin and plugin supply-chain records.

name: Plugin relevance signals: marketplaces declare when a plugin should be suggested (CLI used, host seen, file read, dependency, folder)
what: Marketplace entries can attach matchers so the app suggests a plugin when the session shows it is relevant: a command was run, a host appeared in shell commands, a file matching a glob was read, a dependency appears in a package manifest, or the working directory is under a path; the prompt reads as 'Working with {topic}?'.
how: xge: topic (max 64 characters, defaults to the capitalised plugin name) and signals bge: cli (first command tokens, up to 10), hosts (exact lowercase hostnames seen in URLs in bash commands, up to 20), filesRead (globs against read paths, up to 10), manifestDeps (pairs of file-name regex and declaration regex evaluated against manifests read this session, up to 10), cwd (globs against the working directory relative to the repo root and absolute, up to 10; known at session start so a suggestion can appear before the first turn). Related discovery tools (suggest_plugin_install, suggest_connectors, suggest_skills) only propose; installation goes through user cards and org allowlists.
verevonRelevance: Context-triggered suggestions of connectors and skills ('you ran stripe, install the Stripe plugin') can be expressed declaratively in a registry and evaluated locally without sending file content anywhere.
notes: Where the signals are evaluated (CLI or desktop) was not traced.

name: Mods: in-process plugin handlers with a statically listable capability surface, enabled per session and ordered by admins
what: A plugin can ship a JavaScript module that runs inside the agent process and registers event handlers (tool calls, prompts, turns, interface drawing); everything it can do goes through a mods API, so the file can be scanned before installation to list the events it hooks and calls it makes, and admins can restrict or order which mods load.
how: hooks.json may name one hooks module (modules: at most one path) exporting register(on); the module and its imports must have code-like file names and are treated as ES modules; 'what it hooks and calls is read from its source before it loads; claude plugin validate shows the result'. A manifest types field names a .d.ts contract so one mod can depend on another's added API. The desktop turns the runtime on per session (CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1) and arms a desktop-provided plugin through plugin options (the 'asides' helper; purpose inferred from the name). Managed settings prependPlugins and appendPlugins order managed plugins around user and built-in ones; the built-in guard cc-plugin-sec-default seats itself outermost on managed machines and for Team and Enterprise organisations unless the list is set. Public docs add allowManagedModsOnly, a safe mode flag, disableAllHooks, a statement that mods are not sandboxed and run with the user's permissions, that a mod can approve a tool call before the user is asked, and that mods cannot restyle the permission prompt.
evidence: DOC: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/mods/overview (mods run inside Claude Code; not sandboxed; claude plugin validate lists hooks and calls; allowManagedModsOnly; cannot change the permission prompt)
verevonRelevance: An extension model where all side effects pass through a declared API (so a static scan can show a capability manifest) is a strong pattern for Verevon agent plugins; pair it with admin ordering of managed handlers and a fixed, non-skinnable approval prompt.
notes: The sibling runtime record on EngineSurface covers the UI protocol; this record covers the code-loading model, listability and admin ordering.

name: MCP scope precedence, project-server approval, connector org controls, tool search and output limits (documented, with local settings)
what: MCP servers come from local, project, user, plugin, claude.ai and managed sources with a fixed precedence; project servers need explicit approval before use; admins can force 'ask' or 'blocked' on connector tools; tool definitions load on demand through tool search; very large tool outputs are spilled to files.
how: DOC: scopes local (default, private), project (.mcp.json), user, plugin, claude.ai connectors, with managed settings ranking above all; interactive sessions ask to approve each project-scoped server (reset with claude mcp reset-project-choices), headless and SDK runs need disabledMcpjsonServers or strict MCP config, and a cloned repository cannot approve its own servers in an untrusted folder; connector 'ask' prompts on every call even in auto-accept modes and offers no remember option, 'blocked' removes the tool; tool search is on by default and loads definitions on demand; output over 10,000 tokens warns, default maximum 25,000 tokens (MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS), text over 50,000 characters is saved to a file unless the server raises the limit per tool with the anthropic/maxResultSizeChars annotation up to 500,000; OAuth supports dynamic client registration and client ID metadata documents with authServerMetadataUrl override. SRC: the settings schema carries enableAllProjectMcpServers, enabledMcpjsonServers, disabledMcpjsonServers, allowManagedMcpServersOnly, allowedMcpServers, deniedMcpServers, disableClaudeAiConnectors and managedMcpServers (http and sse only for managed entries, no commands, no ${VAR} references).
verevonRelevance: Adopt the same layering (managed above user above project), trust-on-first-use approval for repository-supplied servers, and per-tool ask/blocked overrides, plus a result-size policy that spills big outputs to files instead of the context window.
notes: Primary provenance is DOC; the SRC settings keys corroborate the documented controls.

name: Electron fuse hardening and embedded ASAR integrity on the shipped Windows binary
what: The shipped claude.exe (Electron 44.4.3) has Node-as-runtime, NODE_OPTIONS and inspector flags switched off, cookie encryption on, app code restricted to the ASAR, and an embedded integrity digest for resources/app.asar that Electron validates at load.
how: REA inspect_pe_resources on claude.exe found an INTEGRITY/ELECTRONASAR resource (122-byte payload at file offset 245154832) whose JSON lists resources\app.asar with alg SHA256 and a header digest. A direct byte read of the executable (read-only) located the fuse sentinel at offset 199378104 followed by schema version 1, fuse count 9 and the wire 010011011. Mapped in the order the public Electron fuse documentation lists them: RunAsNode off, EnableCookieEncryption on, EnableNodeOptionsEnvironmentVariable off, EnableNodeCliInspectArguments off, EnableEmbeddedAsarIntegrityValidation on, OnlyLoadAppFromAsar on, LoadBrowserProcessSpecificV8Snapshot off, GrantFileProtocolExtraPrivileges on (the default; the app still loads some local file: pages), WasmTrapHandlers on. The package manifest lists @electron/fuses and the Forge fuses plugin as build tools.
evidence: REA ev_da0c1d6fc37369a429db6c8d6ce05ed6d4a966f99330ad7b61c267e4d8c667c5 (inspect_pe_resources on claude.exe: PE32+, 246,402,896 bytes, sha256 0109485c3812fa9c6fbc8bfd1c9c390dad4d25a538bbbd0d95e8286283a94bfb; INTEGRITY/ELECTRONASAR resource)
SRC: C:/Program Files/WindowsApps/Claude_2.31226.1.0_x64__pzs8sxrjxfjjc/app/claude.exe fuse sentinel at byte offset 199378104 (wire 010011011) and app/version file (44.4.3)
verevonRelevance: If Verevon ships a desktop shell (Tauri or Electron), turn off run-as-node and inspector fuses, pin the app archive with an embedded digest, and restrict code loading to the packaged archive.
notes: High confidence for the byte values and the integrity resource; medium for the fuse-to-index mapping because the order was taken from the public documentation page rather than from the fuses package. Production hardening is only as strong as OS-level protection of the install directory (MSIX under WindowsApps is read-only for users).

name: Documented auto-mode decision order, fallbacks and classifier inputs (what the classifier sees and when it pauses)
what: Anthropic's public documentation specifies the auto-mode pipeline the desktop relies on: rules first, then read-only and in-folder edits, then the classifier; the classifier sees user messages, non-read-only tool calls and project instructions but not tool results; repeated blocks pause auto mode; an unreachable or silent classifier denies rather than allows.
how: Decision order: allow, ask and deny rules resolve first (exceptions route protected-path writes, critical-path removals, requiresUserInteraction MCP tools, org 'ask' connector tools and per-command network allowances to a prompt or the classifier); read-only actions and edits inside the working directory are approved except protected paths and the first read outside the working directories; everything else goes to the classifier; when it blocks, Claude receives the matched rule name. On entering auto mode broad allow rules that grant arbitrary code execution (Bash(*), wildcard interpreters, package-manager runs, Agent, Monitor) are dropped and restored on exit. Classifier inputs exclude tool results; a PostToolUse hook may attach classifierContext; a server-side probe scans incoming tool results; the server can review actions as part of normal model requests, and no verdict means deny. Fallbacks: 3 consecutive or 20 total blocks pause auto mode and resume prompting (not configurable); boundaries stated in conversation are re-read from the transcript each check and can be lost to compaction (use deny rules for hard guarantees). Subagent work is checked at spawn, per action and at completion. autoMode is read from user settings, managed settings and --settings, never from project settings; precedence is hard_deny, soft_deny, allow exceptions, explicit user intent; classifyAllShell routes every shell command through the classifier; permissions.deny blocks before the classifier and cannot be overridden.
evidence: DOC: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes (how the classifier evaluates actions; repeated-block thresholds; boundaries and approvals stated in conversation; subagent checkpoints)
DOC: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config (autoMode scopes, $defaults, precedence tiers, classifyAllShell, auto-mode CLI subcommands)
verevonRelevance: This is a ready specification for a Model Plane 'autonomy governor': deterministic rules first, a result-blind action classifier second, hard thresholds that hand control back to a human, and org-only policy sources for classifier configuration.
notes: Public docs were read via WebFetch on 2026-10-13; version numbers quoted there (for example v2.1.236 for classifierContext) were not re-verified locally. The desktop-side half of this design is in the host-authored classifier policy and stand-down records.

name: Worktree write guard: a PreToolUse hook that keeps a session's file edits inside its own git worktree
what: Code sessions that run in an isolated git worktree cannot write to the base checkout, to sibling worktrees, to the shared .claude folder, or to the worktree through odd path spellings (Windows short names, UNC or WSL shares, IP-addressed shares, /proc and /dev/fd forms); each block explains where the file should go instead.
how: createBaseHooks registers a PreToolUse hook on the file-edit tools that calls the evaluator (Qs for one worktree, ec for sibling and external containers): paths longer than 8192 characters, Windows unsafe segments (8.3 names, device prefixes, alternate-stream colons), unanchored relative paths when the session cwd cannot be canonicalised, per-process path spellings on POSIX (/proc, /dev/fd, /dev/std*, volume or file ids) and aliases of the worktree under another spelling are blocked with an instructive reason; targets classified as alias_spelling, win32_unsafe_segment, unanchored_relative, base_checkout, sibling_worktree, base_claude_dir and shared_claude_dir (a session that only shares a worktree may not edit the owner's .claude settings). Shared-worktree resolution failures ('unresolved' or 'left') block writes, lazy-worktree sessions use a separate containment check (Ac), and every block logs and emits desktop_ccd_worktree_write_guard_blocked. The guard sits beside the allowed-workspace-folders deny hook (AWF), the project-config-root fence hook, and an unattended-session SendMessage guard in one PreToolUse chain.
verevonRelevance: Verevon sandboxes should enforce workspace confinement at the tool boundary with path canonicalisation that understands Windows aliases and shared-checkout cases, and return model-readable corrective guidance rather than a bare denial.
notes: The Cowork VM path-confinement hook is covered by a sibling record; this guard is the host-side Code equivalent.

name: Desktop-registered PreToolUse hook chain as the app's policy enforcement and input-canonicalisation point
what: Besides prompting through canUseTool, the desktop registers PreToolUse hooks with the engine; they deny contested server names, unattended or malformed calls, rewrite inputs into canonical forms before approval, and answer allow or deny on behalf of the stand-down verdict so the engine never prompts for calls the app already decided.
how: PreToolUse array built in createBaseHooks: (1) allowed-workspace-folders deny for file tools, (2) worktree write guard, (3) project-config-root fence (30 s timeout on SSH) that blocks writes to fenced configuration files with reason project_config_root_fenced, (4) a guard that denies SendMessage aimed at another session (a path, socket or local session id) from a session nobody opened in the app, pointing the agent to the send_message tool, (5) a catch-all hook whose matcher joins every desktop-control tool name (and, for SSH, hosted MCP server tools) which denies calls to servers whose name is contested between an admin and a built-in, requires explicit session ids for lifecycle tools, denies unattended PR monitoring, validates canonical hand-off inputs, and consults forceAskVerdict: when the verdict stands down it emits the stand-down telemetry, notes a consent record for the tool-use id and passes the canonicalised input on (the final allow or deny shape was only partly read); delegated turns are answered by asDelegatedAllow. Hooks return hookSpecificOutput {hookEventName:'PreToolUse', permissionDecision, permissionDecisionReason, updatedInput}.
