name: Typed user-dialog broker: engine-requested dialogs with capability negotiation, sanitised payloads and enforced choice lists
what: Beyond tool approvals, the engine can ask the desktop to show typed dialogs (model-refusal fallback, auto-mode server fallback, chat-thread consent and offer, unattended-consent prompts); the desktop declares which dialog kinds it supports, sanitises every payload, and accepts only answers from the allowed choice list for the right session and prompt.
how: supportedDialogKinds(...) is sent as an SDK option so the engine only requests kinds the UI can render: refusal_fallback_prompt always, auto_mode_server_fallback when enabled, the chat-binding consent and offer kinds when the module loaded, and registered prompt kinds that are enabled. createOnUserDialog(sessionId) returns the handler for the request_user_dialog control request: it parses the payload per kind (malformed, unsupported or already-aborted requests resolve as {behavior:'cancelled'}), assigns a random promptId, stores the pending prompt with a response timeout, emits an opened event and settles on abort. Payload sanitising: strings are length-capped (title 512, paragraphs 2048 each and at most 8, gateway host 256) and cleaned of invisible characters while keeping legibility joiners; a help URL is kept only if it is https on claude.com or anthropic.com and at most 2048 characters. respond(sessionId, promptId, choice, kind) succeeds only when the pending prompt belongs to that session and kind and the choice is in validChoices (or 'cancelled'); unknown choices are logged and rejected; prompts with a confirmAnswer hook use a two-step respondConfirmed with an in-flight counter.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane should negotiate which interactive dialog kinds the client supports, validate and sanitise every dialog payload from the engine, and bind each answer to a session, a kind and an enumerated choice set.

name: Side chats as read-only forks: deny-all prompter, closed tool-input schemas, cwd read confinement and a breach detector
what: A side chat (a question asked without disturbing the main thread) runs as a non-persistent fork of the conversation that can only Read, Grep and Glob inside the session folder; it cannot prompt for approvals, its tool inputs are validated against a closed key set per tool, and if a tool result ever arrives for something the guard should have refused the side chat is stopped and a breach event is logged.
how: spawnReadOnlyFork builds SDK options with persistSession false, tools limited to the read list (or none for the no-tools variant, whose system prompt says the fork has no tools), settingSources [] so no repository settings apply, permissionMode default, an env scrub list, and a canUseTool that always denies (either 'requires per-call approval under the organization's tool policy, which side chats cannot prompt for' or 'Side chats only read inside the session's working folder'). A PreToolUse hook (YU/XU) allows only Read, Grep, Glob (and ToolSearch when no folder is set), rejects any input key outside a per-tool allowlist, requires string path fields, confines paths to the working directory through a canonicalising resolver, and rejects Glob patterns that put '..' after a wildcard or use brace, comma or bracket forms the matcher cannot canonicalise; any guard error denies with a generic reason (fail closed). When the fork would be started with the parent's tool list ('declare parent tools' mode) the code verifies the guard, default permission mode and simple-mode flag are all present and otherwise falls back to Read, Grep and Glob only (telemetry desktop_ccd_side_chat_tools_narrowed). While streaming, a user message carrying a tool result for a tool the guard should have refused triggers desktop_ccd_side_chat_guard_breach, an error to the UI and stopSideChat. Forks also honour a token-cap window (in-memory trip and persisted window) and refuse to start when it is exceeded.
verevonRelevance: Helper or side agents in Verevon should run with a closed tool set, a deny-all approval channel, per-tool input schemas, path confinement and an after-the-fact breach detector, and should be unable to inherit repository-level settings.
notes: Defence in depth is explicit in the code comments: the guard is the control and the breach detector exists because 'this should never happen'.

name: Closed-vocabulary telemetry for approval routing: 165 permission-broker events and a named reason for every auto-deny
what: The permission broker emits structured events for every automatic decision, so operators can see why a call was refused or allowed without reading content: 38 auto-deny call sites with 24 literal reason codes (forged card name, internal name not served by app, unattended simulator or move to cloud or setting change or send-message or PR monitor, contested server name, project-config fence, handoff and storage prechecks, scheduled-store states and others), auto-allow events with a reason, delegated-ask allows, decision-reason cache hits, fan-out gating and worktree-guard blocks.
